data.title: Coinbase Global jumps 12% after on regulatory win for tokenized stock trading
data.description:
Coinbase Global (COIN) climbed about 12% on Friday, after the SEC approved a temporary "Innovation Exemption" creating a regulatory pathway for certain platforms to facilitate trading in tokenized U.S.-listed securities. Coinbase was among the crypto-related stocks that extended gains following the announcement.

The advance built on a 6% gain the previous session. data.title: 'Calmer heads' to start driving price discovery next week: SA analyst
data.description:
Following a week of chaotic market volatility driven by the Federal Reserve and a quarterly triple-witching event, investors can expect calmer heads to drive price discovery starting next week, according to Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research.

King anticipates that as the reactionary trading subsides, a stark divergence in sector performance will emerge looking toward the year's end. Semiconductors (SMH up 57% YTD) and the tech-heavy Nasdaq (QQQ up 17% YTD) are expected to build on their gains, while crypto (IBIT down 11% YTD) is positioned well for a turnaround.

Conversely, the SA analyst forecasts that older-economy proxies like industrials (XLI up 9% YTD) and the Dow Jones (DIA up 7% YTD) may struggle to keep pace. Bonds (SHY) (TLT) (IEF) (ZROZ), meanwhile, will "probably start to surprise to the upside."

"Next week we will see calmer heads begin the process of price discovery into year end," King said.

Meanwhile, the stock market ended mixed Friday as Treasury yields reversed Thursday's retreat, with the 10-year note (US10Y) climbing back to the key 5.0% mark.

The S&P 500 (SP500) +0.2%, the Dow (DJI) -0.2%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +0.4%.

data.title: Navient completes $612.5M securitization backed by private education loans
data.description:
Navient (NAVI)  closed its $612.5M Navient Private Education Loan Trust (NAVSL) 2026-A transaction, its fourth student loan securitization this year, the company said Friday.

The deal is Navient's (NAVI) first designed to support investment by investors subject to European Union’s securitization regulation and the United Kingdom’s securitization regulatory framework.

"Expanding access to our securitizations for investors operating under EU and UK regulatory frameworks reflects our ongoing commitment to the capital markets," said Chief Financial Officer Steve Hauber.

Navient (NAVI) agreed to keep a portion of the notes and certificates on terms designed to align with the risk retention requirements of the EU securitization regulation and the UK securitization regulatory framework and support the compliance needs of investors subject to EU or UK requirements.

Navient (NAVI) stock fell 3.4% in Friday regular-hours trading.

The securitization's book runner is J.P. Morgan (JPM).

data.title: Wall Street closes mixed as Treasury yields rebound
data.description:
The stock market ended mixed Friday as Treasury yields reversed Thursday's retreat, with the 10-year note climbing back to the key 5.0% mark.

The S&P 500 (SP500) +0.2%, the Dow (DJI) -0.2%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +0.4%.

Information technology (XLK) (+0.8%) and industrials (XLI) (+0.5%) led the market's gains, while utilities (XLU) (-1.4%) and materials (XLB) (-1.1%) lagged as the day's biggest decliners.

The stock market rebounded Thursday after Wednesday's selloff, which followed the Federal Reserve's first rate hike since 2023.

“This was a week of chaotic volatility in securities markets, a result of back-to-back FOMC and quarterly triple-witching events," said Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research. "Next week we will see calmer heads begin the process of price discovery into year end.”

Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said he supported the central bank's decision earlier this week to hike rates as inflation has outpaced the Fed's 2% goal for more than five years.

Elsewhere on the economic calendar, industrial production growth stalled in August, falling short of expectations, while August leading indicators slipped and missed the consensus.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) rose nine basis points to 4.77%, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) increased seven basis points to 5.01%, and the 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) advanced four basis points to 5.34%.

data.title: U.S. drilling rig count jumps by 4 in latest Baker Hughes survey
data.description:
The number of oil and gas rigs actively drilling in the U.S. rose by 4 to 595, Baker Hughes reported Friday in its latest weekly survey.

The number of active drilling rigs targeting crude oil in the U.S. gained rose by 2 to 452 in the week ended September 18, while gas rigs gained 2 to 134 and miscellaneous rigs remained unchanged at 9.

The total rig count was up by 53, or 9.8%, compared to the same time last year, while the number of rigs drilling for oil rose by 34, or 8.1%, from a year ago, and gas rigs gained 16, or 13.5%, from a year earlier.

Rigs targeting oil in the Permian Basin added 1 to 268 during the past week, while the Eagle Ford count stayed flat at 42 and the Williston Basin gained 1 to 30.

data.title: Fluence Energy falls again as Jefferies downgrades on weaker outlook
data.description:
Fluence Energy (FLNC) falls 4.2% in Friday's trading as Jefferies downgraded shares to Hold from Buy with a $7 price target, slashed from $19, anticipating "a challenging path forward" amid new questions about future customer confidence and liquidity after the energy storage company cut revenue guidance just six weeks after the most recent reset on the FQ3 earnings conference call.

Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith said he is awaiting "proofpoints on execution post a series of issues at the Houston manufacturing facility," primarily concerned with the impact on customer relationships and long-term market share as a result of recent missteps.

The analyst said he expected 45% Y/Y revenue growth and positive EBITDA in FY 2026 when he upgraded the stock in February, but he now expects just 6% revenue growth and a $200M EBITDA loss.

"Execution risk is clearly higher than assumed, with FY26 estimates now materially lower and meaningfully less confidence in the FY27 [and beyond] fundamental story," and near-term hurdles are significant given the liquidity and history of missed expectations, Dumoulin-Smith said.

Fluence (FLNC) also was downgraded at Goldman Sachs and Baird earlier this week following the guidance cut.

data.title: DOJ considers joining Texas BlackRock, State Street anitrust case - report
data.description:
The U.S. Department of Justice is evaluating joining a state-led antitrust lawsuit against BlackRock (BLK) and State Street (STT) concerning claims that the fund managers used their power to pressure coal producers to cut output. 

Senior DOJ officials have discussed the possibility of joining the lawsuits with the states recently, according to a  Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. No final decisions have been made and the regulator may decide not to do anything.

In November 2024, Texas and 10 other Republican state attorneys general sued BlackRock (BLK) and State Street (STT), claiming that the money managers pressured coal producers to cut output causing residents to pay higher power bills.

Vanguard Group, which was originally named as a defendant in the suit, settled this February, agreeing to pay $29.5 million and to stop imposing ESG goals for its investments. 

The DOJ declined to comment on if it will join the lawsuit, but told Bloomberg it's focused on “affordability for all Americans across our economy.” The Texas attorney general’s office didn’t respond to a request for comment. BlackRock declined to comment and referred to an earlier statement calling the suit "baseless."  State Street also declined to comment and said the "lawsuit remains baseless and without merit.”

data.title: Trump announces White House ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico
data.description:
US President Donald Trump said he was banning CNN (WBD), MS NOW (VSNT) and Politico from the White House, accusing outlets of repeatedly publishing what he called “FAKE NEWS” about his administration and the country.

In a Friday Truth Social post, Trump said the ban was effective immediately and suggested other media organizations could face similar action.

Trump also criticized Politico over what he described as an $8 million subscription from the US government under former President Joe Biden, calling the payment “illegal and ridiculous” and saying it appeared to him to be corruption.

“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America,” Trump wrote.

He did not provide further details in the post about how the ban would be implemented or what specific reports from the three outlets prompted the action.

Trump referred to MS NOW (VSNT) as having recently changed its name from MSNBC, saying the change followed a lack of viewership and credibility. He concluded by saying other media outlets he considers “Fake News Media Outlets” could be targeted next.

The post did not provide additional information about the scope of the restrictions or how they would affect the outlets’ coverage of the White House.
